<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

Every same-repo PR currently runs all 9 NPU a3 suites (base-b 1/2/4/8/16, base-c
acc/perf 2/16) in full on scarce self-hosted Atlas 800T runners, even when the
change touches a narrow code slice. The coverage infrastructure to do better
already exists (per-test coverage collection, test_case_map, test_selector), but
it could not actually drive PR runs:

- `recommend-tests-from-coverage` was hard-disabled (`if: false`, OBS baseline
  returned 403) and its recommendations were never wired into the real test
  jobs — no per-suite bucketing, no filtering, no skip semantics.
- The baseline was incomplete: server / scheduler / detokenizer subprocesses
  were untraced (subprocess coverage had been removed pending a graceful
  teardown story), and the base-a CPU unit suite contributed no coverage, so
  recommendations systematically missed server-side code paths.
- `test_selector.py` only recognized the k8s workspace prefix, silently
  discarding test cases collected under other runner topologies, and
  parametrized pytest node ids were mangled by the filesystem-safe encoding.
- There was no coverage report to inspect what the baseline actually measures.

This PR closes the loop: NPU PR CI now runs only the coverage-recommended
subset per suite, and the baseline behind those recommendations now includes
subprocess (server-side) code, the base-a unit suite, hosted-runner
collections — and is inspectable via HTML reports.

## Modifications

**Precision test selection (PRs run only the recommended subset)**
- Re-enabled `recommend-tests-from-coverage` in `pr-test-npu.yml` (runs on
  `pull_request` in non-coverage mode). Every step carries step-level
  `continue-on-error: true`, so this advisory job always concludes `success`
  and can never cascade-kill test jobs through the fast-fail health check;
  failed steps stay visible (red ✗ + annotation).
- Added `scripts/ci/npu/precise-test/bucket_recommended_tests.py`: enumerates
  each suite's registered PR-mode tests via `list_tests.py`, intersects with
  the recommendation, and exports per-suite `should_run_<suite>` /
  `only_tests_<suite>` outputs. Empty bucket → skip the whole job (frees a3
  runners); zero-file enumeration falls back to a full run (registered-pool
  guard, no silently green suites); any failure → empty outputs → full-suite
  fallback.
- All base-b / base-c a3 jobs now `needs: recommend-tests-from-coverage`,
  skip on `should_run_* == 'false'`, and pass their bucket via the new
  `only_tests` input.
- `_npu-pr-test-stage.yml` / `_npu-single-node-test-stage.yml`: new
  `only_tests` input; a non-empty list is staged to
  `/tmp/precision_tests.txt` and forwarded as `run_suite.py --only-file-list`;
  coverage job names now include the partition.
- `test/run_suite.py`: new `--only-file-list` (with `load_only_file_list`)
  filters the suite before partitioning, so matrix shards split the filtered
  pool evenly and disjointly.

**Subprocess coverage re-enabled (server / scheduler / detokenizer measured)**
- `run_tests_with_coverage.sh`: exports `COVERAGE_PROCESS_START` and installs
  an inert-by-default `sglang_ci_subprocess_coverage.pth` next to the
  coverage package so Popen'd servers auto-start coverage; subprocess files
  inherit the per-test `COVERAGE_FILE` (parallel mode suffixes them) and land
  in the same per-test dir, so the existing combine / test_case_map logic
  attributes them with zero changes. `CACHE_ROOT` is now overridable via
  `PRECISE_TEST_CACHE_ROOT`.
- `coveragerc`: `sigterm = True` — scheduler/detokenizer have no SIGTERM
  handler of their own; the handler installed by `process_startup()` is what
  flushes their data when teardown SIGTERMs the tree.
- New `precise_test_coverage_plugin.py` pytest plugin, double-gated on
  `SGLANG_KILL_PROCESS_TREE_GRACEFUL=1` and loaded only in coverage runs:
  patches `kill_process_tree` in the pytest process only with a SIGTERM-first
  + bounded-wait (default 20 s) wrapper that defers to the original SIGKILL
  backstop, and refreshes stale bindings across `sys.modules`. No product
  code (`python/sglang`) is modified.
- `setup_coverage` encoding keeps `[` and `]` so parametrized pytest node ids
  (`test_x[case_id]`) stay reversible.

**Baseline completeness & runner generality**
- `test_selector.py`: replaced the hardcoded k8s prefix with
  `WORKSPACE_MARKER = "__sglang__sglang__"`, recognizing both k8s
  (`/__w/sglang/sglang`) and hosted (`/home/runner/work/sglang/sglang`)
  checkout roots via partition at the first anchor.
- New `base-a-test-npu-cov` job in `pr-test-npu.yml`: coverage-mode
  counterpart of the base-a CPU unit gate. Runs on `ubuntu-latest` (the suite
  mocks torch_npu / sgl_kernel_npu and needs a CPU triton; the NPU image's
  triton-ascend conflicts with those mocks), stages coverage under a local
  `PRECISE_TEST_CACHE_ROOT`, and ships it to `setup-covstub` as an artifact
  that merges 1:1 into the shared-disk run dir.
- `setup-covstub` merges that artifact and materializes the git-ignored
  `_version.py` placeholder in covstub so report generation finds all
  recorded sources.

**HTML coverage reports (visibility, non-blocking)**
- New "Generate HTML coverage report" step in `setup-covstub`: combines the
  per-test data (`--keep`) and renders two reports — the full one plus an
  NPU-only view via a dedicated rcfile
  (`source = covstub/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/npu`, full-tree denominator,
  never-imported files count as 0%). Totals are appended to the step summary.
- The step uses `continue-on-error: true` with natural `errexit` propagation:
  a failure shows as a red step but never blocks the baseline
  Archive/Publish/Cleanup pipeline. Reports live outside `outputs/`, are
  uploaded as the `coverage-html-report` artifact, and are published to the
  shared disk as fixed-name `htmlcov.tar.gz` / `htmlcov-npu.tar.gz`
  (latest-run retention, same as the baseline).
- `setup-covstub` and `pr-test-npu-finish` now also wait on
  `base-a-test-npu-cov`.

## Accuracy Tests

<!-- If this pull request affects model outputs (e.g., changes to the kernel or model forward code), provide accuracy test results. -->

## Speed Tests and Profiling

<!-- If this pull request impacts inference speed, provide benchmarking and profiling results. -->

## Checklist

- [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

-# Reusable workflow: cross-reference CI test failures with coverage-based
-# test recommendations. Called by pr-test-npu.yml's analyze-failure-report job.
-name: Analyze Failure Report
-
-on:
-  workflow_call:
-    inputs:
-      log_artifact_pattern:
-        type: string
-        required: true
-        description: 'Glob pattern for test log artifacts (e.g. selected-test-logs-*)'
-      diffusion_artifact_pattern:
-        type: string
-        required: false
-        default: 'diffusion-failures-*'
-        description: 'Glob pattern for diffusion failure artifacts (consistency failures)'
-      recommendations_content:
-        type: string
-        required: false
-        default: ''
-        description: 'Content of recommendations from upstream job output'
-
-defaults:
-  run:
-    shell: bash -el {0}
-
-jobs:
-  analyze:
-    name: cross-reference failures with recommendations
-    continue-on-error: true  # Non-blocking on parse/read failure.
-    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
-    steps:
-      - name: Checkout sglang repo
-        uses: actions/checkout@v4
-
-      # ----- Step 1: Locate recommendations -----
-      - name: Locate recommendations file
-        id: locate-recs
-        run: |
-          mkdir -p ./test-logs
-          # Always create the file so the analyzer can run on diffusion-only failures.
-          touch ./test-logs/_recommended.txt
-          echo "RECS_FILE=./test-logs/_recommended.txt" >> $GITHUB_ENV
-
-          if [ -n "${{ inputs.recommendations_content }}" ]; then
-            echo "has_recommendations=true" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
-            echo "Using workflow output recommendations"
-            echo "${{ inputs.recommendations_content }}" > ./test-logs/_recommended.txt
-            echo "RECS_SOURCE=output" >> $GITHUB_ENV
-            COUNT=$(wc -l < ./test-logs/_recommended.txt)
-            echo "Recommendations count: ${COUNT}"
-          else
-            echo "has_recommendations=false" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
-            echo "RECS_SOURCE=none" >> $GITHUB_ENV
-            echo "::notice::No recommended test cases detected; analyzing log and diffusion failures only."
-          fi
-
-      # ----- Step 2: Download test logs -----
-      # continue-on-error is a step keyword, not a download-artifact input.
-      - name: Download test logs
-        uses: actions/download-artifact@v7
-        with:
-          pattern: ${{ inputs.log_artifact_pattern }}
-          path: ./test-logs
-          merge-multiple: true
-        continue-on-error: true
-
-      # ----- Step 2b: Download diffusion failure artifacts -----
-      # Keep merge-multiple off so each partition's consistency_failures/summary.json
-      # lands in its own <artifact-name>/ directory instead of clobbering the others.
-      - name: Download diffusion failure artifacts
-        uses: actions/download-artifact@v7
-        with:
-          pattern: ${{ inputs.diffusion_artifact_pattern }}
-          path: ./diffusion-failures
-        continue-on-error: true
-
-      - name: Check for diffusion failure artifacts
-        id: check-diffusion
-        run: |
-          if compgen -G "./diffusion-failures/*/consistency_failures/summary.json" > /dev/null; then
-            echo "found=true" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
-            echo "Diffusion consistency failure artifacts found"
-          else
-            echo "found=false" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
-            echo "No diffusion consistency failure artifacts"
-          fi
-
-      - name: Show downloaded artifacts structure
-        run: |
-          echo "Downloaded log files:"
-          find ./test-logs -type f | head -50 || echo "  (no logs found)"
-          echo "Downloaded diffusion failure artifacts:"
-          if compgen -G "./diffusion-failures/*" > /dev/null; then
-            find ./diffusion-failures -type f | head -50
-          else
-            echo "  (no diffusion failure artifacts found)"
-          fi
-
-      # ----- Step 3: Run analysis -----
-      - name: Ensure regex is available
-        if: ${{ steps.locate-recs.outputs.has_recommendations != 'false' || steps.check-diffusion.outputs.found == 'true' }}
-        run: |
-          set -euo pipefail
-          if ! python3 -c "import regex" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
-            echo "regex not found for $(python3 -V); bootstrapping pip and installing regex"
-            curl -fsSL https://bootstrap.pypa.io/get-pip.py -o get-pip.py
-            python3 get-pip.py --break-system-packages
-            python3 -m pip install --break-system-packages regex
-          fi
-          python3 -c "import regex; print('regex ok:', regex.__file__)"
-
-      - name: Run failure analysis
-        if: ${{ steps.locate-recs.outputs.has_recommendations != 'false' || steps.check-diffusion.outputs.found == 'true' }}
-        id: analysis
-        continue-on-error: true
-        run: |
-          python3 scripts/ci/npu/precise-test/analyze_failure_report.py \
-            --log-dir ./test-logs \
-            --diffusion-dir ./diffusion-failures \
-            --recommendations-file "${RECS_FILE}" \
-            --recommendations-source "${RECS_SOURCE:-none}" \
-            --output ./test-logs/failure_report.md
-
-      # ----- Step 4: Upload report -----
-      - name: Upload failure analysis report
-        if: always()
-        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""
+Bucket coverage-recommended tests per CI suite.
+
+Runs after test_selector.py has produced recommended_pytest_paths.txt (one
+pytest path per line, repo-relative, optional ::case suffix). For each
+requested suite, enumerate the suite's registered test files via list_tests.py
+and intersect with the recommended files, then write per-suite GitHub Actions
+step outputs:
+
+    only_tests_<key>   multi-line list of intersected files (repo-relative);
+                       exported non-empty ONLY in precision mode, so callers
+                       can reference it without any extra guard expression
+    should_run_<key>   'false' only when precision mode is active, the suite
+                       enumerated a non-empty registered pool, and this
+                       suite's bucket is empty -> the caller skips the whole
+                       job; 'true' otherwise (including full-suite runs)
+
+Suite keys replace '-' with '_' because GitHub Actions output names must be
+valid shell identifiers. Any failure path yields empty/missing outputs, which
+callers treat as "run the full suite".
+
+Usage:
+    python3 bucket_recommended_tests.py \
+        --recommended recommended_pytest_paths.txt \
+        --suites base-a-test-npu,base-b-test-1-npu-a3 \
+        --precision-mode true \
+        --github-output "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
+"""
+
+import argparse
+import os
+import subprocess
+import sys
+import tempfile
+from pathlib import Path
+
+# Repo layout: this script lives at <repo>/scripts/ci/npu/precise-test/.
+SCRIPT_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
+LIST_TESTS = SCRIPT_DIR / "list_tests.py"
+REPO_ROOT = SCRIPT_DIR.parents[3]
+
+
+def normalize_rel(path: str) -> str:
+    """Normalize a pytest path entry to a repo-relative posix file path.
+
+    Strips an optional ::case suffix and the leading ./, converts absolute
+    paths (any runner topology) to repo-relative.
+    """
+    p = path.strip().replace("\\", "/").removeprefix("./")
+    p = p.split("::", 1)[0]
+    if os.path.isabs(p):
+        p = os.path.relpath(p, REPO_ROOT).replace(os.sep, "/")
+    return p
+
+
+def enumerate_suite_files(suite: str, work_dir: Path) -> list:
+    """List the suite's registered PR-mode test files via list_tests.py."""
+    out_file = work_dir / (suite.replace("-", "_") + ".txt")
+    subprocess.run(
+        [
+            sys.executable,
+            str(LIST_TESTS),
+            "--hw",
+            "npu",
+            "--suite",
+            suite,
+            "-o",
+            str(out_file),
+        ],
+        check=True,
+    )
+    with open(out_file) as f:
+        return [line.strip() for line in f if line.strip()]
+
+
+def main():
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
+        description="Bucket coverage-recommended tests per CI suite."
+    )
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--recommended",
+        type=str,
+        default=str(SCRIPT_DIR / "recommended_pytest_paths.txt"),
+        help="recommended_pytest_paths.txt written by test_selector.py",
+    )
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--suites",
+        type=str,
+        required=True,
+        help="Comma-separated suite names to bucket (e.g. base-a-test-npu,base-b-test-1-npu-a3)",
+    )
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--precision-mode",
+        type=str,
+        default="false",
+        help="'true' to enable precision mode (run only the recommended tests)",
+    )
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--github-output",
+        type=str,
+        default="",
+        help="GITHUB_OUTPUT file to write step outputs to (empty = print only)",
+    )
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+
+    # Recommended set: file-level, repo-relative.
+    rec_file = Path(args.recommended)
+    recommended = set()
+    if rec_file.exists():
+        with open(rec_file) as f:
+            recommended = {
+                normalize_rel(line)
+                for line in f
+                if line.strip() and not line.startswith("ERROR")
+            }
+    else:
+        print(f"::warning::Recommended file not found: {rec_file}")
+    print(f"Recommended test files: {len(recommended)}")
+
+    suites = [s.strip() for s in args.suites.split(",") if s.strip()]
+    work_dir = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="bucket_tests_"))
+
+    buckets = {}
+    # Registered-pool size per suite. An empty ENUMERATION (0 files) must
+    # never let precision mode skip the whole job — that would silently drop
+    # the suite from the PR gate — so the output loop falls back to a
+    # full-suite run in that case.
+    suite_pool_sizes = {}
+    for suite in suites:
+        suite_files = {normalize_rel(f) for f in enumerate_suite_files(suite, work_dir)}
+        suite_pool_sizes[suite] = len(suite_files)
+        if not suite_files:
+            print(f"::warning::Suite {suite}: enumerated 0 registered test files")
+        intersection = sorted(suite_files & recommended)
+        buckets[suite] = intersection
+        print(
+            f"Suite {suite}: {len(suite_files)} files, {len(intersection)} recommended"
+        )
+
+    total_count = sum(len(b) for b in buckets.values())
+    precision_mode = args.precision_mode == "true" and total_count > 0
+    print(f"total_count={total_count} precision_mode={precision_mode}")
+
+    if not args.github_output:
+        return
+
+    with open(args.github_output, "a") as out:
+        for suite, files in buckets.items():
+            key = suite.replace("-", "_")
+            # Gate bucket contents on precision_mode: a run without precision
+            # mode enabled never exports a non-empty bucket, so downstream
+            # jobs can reference only_tests_<key> without any extra guard
+            # expression.
+            bucket_files = files if precision_mode else []
+            out.write(f"only_tests_{key}<<EOF\n")
+            for line in bucket_files:
+                out.write(line + "\n")
+            out.write("EOF\n")
+            # 'false' ONLY when precision mode is on, the suite enumerated a
+            # non-empty registered pool, and this bucket is empty -> the
+            # caller skips the whole suite job. An empty ENUMERATION (0
+            # registered files, e.g. a list_tests/run_suite filter drift)
+            # falls back to 'true' so the job runs the full suite instead of
+            # silently vanishing. Anything else ('true', or a missing output
+            # from a failed step) means full-suite run.
+            should_run = (
+                "false"
+                if (precision_mode and suite_pool_sizes[suite] and not files)
+                else "true"
+            )
+            out.write(f"should_run_{key}={should_run}\n")
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()
